title: claude-profiles registry
description: The contract shared by the bash implementation (lib/registry.sh) and the PowerShell module (powershell/ClaudeProfiles). Neither reads this file at runtime — it is documentation for humans and the fixture that tests/registry-contract.sh checks both implementations against. Keep it in step with reg_sort_children() in lib/registry.sh, which defines the canonical key order.

version.description: Registry format version. A reader that does not recognise the value must refuse to run rather than guess.

profiles.description: Keyed by profile name. The primary account is never listed here — it is the account that uses every default location and is deliberately unmanaged.

propertyNames.description: Lowercase letters, digits, hyphen and underscore. No dots: the registry's internal flat-path format is dot-delimited. Reserved names are rejected because a profile called 'primary' would make every error message ambiguous. The character set is also the sanitisation boundary for .claude-profile files, which arrive inside cloned repositories and are therefore untrusted.

cli.description: Present when the profile manages a Claude Code CLI account. Absent for a desktop-only profile.

configDir.description: Value for CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR. Stored with a leading ~ where possible so a synced dotfiles repo is portable. Must never equal ~/.claude, which belongs to the primary account.

auth.description: config-dir: CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR alone isolates the login, because on Linux and Windows .credentials.json lives inside that directory. oauth-token: additionally supply CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, which is required on macOS because the login lives in a single shared Keychain item that CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR does not separate.

tokenBackend.description: Where the OAuth token is stored. Only meaningful when auth is oauth-token. 'file' is a mode-0600 fallback used only where no OS secret store is available, and the tool says so out loud when it writes one.

tokenCreated.description: Date the token was generated. Tokens from `claude setup-token` last one year; the shell integration starts warning at day 335.

desktop.description: Present when the profile manages a Claude desktop instance. Absent for a CLI-only profile.

userDataDir.description: Value passed to Electron's --user-data-dir. Everything the instance stores — the encrypted credential blob, MCP config, window state, caches — lands here. Must never equal the primary profile's directory.

appPath.description: The application binary or bundle this profile launches. Normally the single installed Claude app, shared by every profile. It differs only when the profile uses a mirrored copy.

mirrored.description: Whether appPath is a mirrored copy rather than the real install. Stored as a string so both implementations serialize it identically. A mirror is a frozen snapshot that does not auto-update; doctor reports how stale it is. macOS needs one only when the Keychain round-trip test fails; Windows needs one whenever the install is MSIX, because Windows refuses to execute anything directly out of C:\Program Files\WindowsApps and the --user-data-dir flag therefore cannot be passed.

launcher.description: Path to the generated launcher, if one was installed: a .app bundle on macOS, a .lnk shortcut on Windows, a .desktop entry on Linux. Recorded so uninstall can find it.

description.description: Free text shown by `claude-profiles list`. Purely for humans.
